question: Should OpenClaw add a core child-visible pre-timeout warning/grace contract for sub-agent runs, and what config/tool surface and native/ACP delivery semantics should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public config/API semantics, default behavior, and cross-runtime lifecycle behavior that automation should not invent.

options.title: Define Core Warning Contract
options.body: Add a documented config-level grace setting, and optionally a carefully named per-spawn override, with native and ACP warning delivery covered by lifecycle tests.

options.title: Keep Hard Timeout And Improve Recovery
options.body: Decline pre-timeout child warnings for now and focus on post-timeout notification, durable completion delivery, and recovery issues instead.

options.title: Document Prompt Checkpointing Only
options.body: Document operator prompting/checkpoint guidance without adding new runtime config or warning delivery behavior.

recommendation.title: Define Core Warning Contract
recommendation.body: Add a documented config-level grace setting, and optionally a carefully named per-spawn override, with native and ACP warning delivery covered by lifecycle tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent review and source-history signal around subagent lifecycle and timeout semantics.
